items.headline: Long-end Treasury stress becomes the dominant macro signal as oil and Hormuz lift inflation risk
items.summary: On 18 August the U.S. 30-year Treasury yield reached about 5.33%, its highest level since 2007, while the 10-year traded near 4.74%. Brent moved above USD 90 as hopes for a near-term U.S.-Iran settlement faded and Hormuz remained constrained.
items.whyItMatters: The market is now experiencing weaker growth data and higher long-end yields at the same time. AGCI treats this as a term-premium and inflation-risk warning rather than a simple monetary-policy signal. It raises the hurdle rate for long-duration equities, leveraged real estate and capital-intensive AI projects.
items.agciSignal: LONG-END YIELD SHOCK / OIL-INFLATION RISK / REDUCE DURATION COMPLACENCY

items.headline: Barron's flags 30-year yield stress, AI capital intensity and renewed chip dispersion
items.summary: New Barron's newsletters received after the prior cutoff emphasized the 30-year Treasury yield at its highest since 2007, heavy AI spending at Amazon and Meta, Nvidia/OpenAI data-center economics, Micron's memory-cycle momentum and continued debate over whether high AI investment can earn adequate returns.
items.whyItMatters: These stories reinforce an existing AGCI distinction: AI demand can remain structurally strong while financing conditions deteriorate. The correct response is not to abandon AI exposure, but to demand stronger free-cash-flow coverage, lower refinancing dependence and wider valuation margins.
items.agciSignal: AI STRUCTURAL DEMAND / FINANCING QUALITY MATTERS MORE

items.headline: Home Depot beats Q2 sales expectations but housing-sensitive demand remains constrained
items.summary: Home Depot reported second-quarter sales above expectations and shares rose premarket, but the broader housing backdrop remains weak and management kept its full-year outlook unchanged. Smaller projects improved while large-ticket activity remained pressured by elevated borrowing costs and affordability constraints.
items.whyItMatters: The result does not justify relaxing AGCI real-estate underwriting. It supports the view that repair-and-maintenance demand is resilient, while transaction-driven housing activity and large discretionary projects remain rate-sensitive.
items.agciSignal: HOUSING DEMAND RESILIENT AT THE MARGIN / LARGE PROJECTS STILL RATE-CONSTRAINED

items.headline: Greed eases slightly to 90 but remains extreme against Valuation 85
items.summary: The 18 August AGCI snapshot shows Greed 90/100, Valuation 85/100, Mid Bull regime and confidence 73/100. Greed is down two points on the day but the condition remains EUPHORIA_RISK with the directive 'Capital preservation / Do not chase'.
items.whyItMatters: A two-point decline in Greed is not enough to neutralize the valuation and macro warning. With long yields rising and oil above USD 90, cash optionality and staged entries remain more valuable than chasing momentum.
items.agciSignal: EXTREME GREED + EXTREME VALUATION / DO NOT CHASE

items.headline: Industrial production is due today; FOMC minutes follow on 19 August
items.summary: The Federal Reserve's official calendar schedules industrial production for 18 August and the minutes of the 28-29 July FOMC meeting for 19 August.
items.whyItMatters: The data sequence can test whether the current combination of soft consumption, elevated energy prices and rising long-term yields is becoming a stagflationary mix or remains a temporary market dislocation.
items.agciSignal: MACRO CONFIRMATION PENDING / FOMC MINUTES HIGH IMPORTANCE
